title: How GPS depends on Einstein
summary: Position from time signals, why the receiver solves for its own clock bias, the special and general relativistic clock shifts (-7 and +45 microseconds per day), the factory frequency offset, the eccentricity and Sagnac corrections, and ionospheric delay.
questions: Why does a receiver need four satellites rather than three, and what extra thing does it get?
Which relativistic effect is larger for GPS satellites, and which direction does the net effect push their clocks?
If every satellite clock ran fast by the same amount, why would position not drift 10 km a day, and why is relativity still essential?
Why can't the factory frequency offset handle the eccentricity correction, and where is it applied instead?
How does a dual-frequency receiver remove most of the ionospheric delay?
